source_metadata.title: When Experience Becomes Instruction: Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems
source_metadata.input_file: When Experience Becomes Instruction Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems - 2608.05563v2.pdf

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluates whether bounded attacker-controlled trajectories can poison the experience-to-instruction promotion process in trajectory-grounded self-evolving skill systems and identifies the conditions under which target behavior is promoted into a persistent skill artifact.

The primary attacker model is skill-visible black-box: an attacker may inspect public or installed target skills and contribute a bounded share of trajectories, but cannot inspect private trajectory pools, filters, evolution prompts, or directly modify the skill bank.

The authors abstract a trajectory-based self-evolving skill system as a trajectory pool T, quality filter or router F, LLM-backed evolver E, and versioned skill bank S, with evolution updating the bank from filtered trajectory evidence and the current skill state.

Artifact poisoning success is defined as the conjunction of Inclusion, Evolution Attribution, and Realization: poisoned records must enter an evolver-consumable stream, be treated as reusable skill-worthy evidence, and survive synthesis into the generated skill.

Skill Embedding Rate (SER) is the primary poisoning metric and is the fraction of completed evolution trials in which a behavior-specific, diff-aware rule detects newly added target behavior in the output skill.

outcome.definition: Fraction of completed evolution trials with newly embedded target behavior detected by a pre-registered behavior-specific diff-aware rule.

atoms.canonical_statement: The initial skill is checked before SER scoring so pre-existing target text is not counted; LLM judge outputs are used only to inspect ambiguous cases and do not define poisoning success.
Hard and Soft spreadsheet task accuracy are reported only as a skill-usefulness sanity check and are explicitly separated from the artifact-poisoning metric.
The empirical scope measures generated skill artifacts rather than downstream trigger activation, action execution, real credential theft, exfiltration, or destructive effects.

The empirical claims cover trajectory-grounded artifact evolution in SkillClaw and a structural transfer case in Trace2Skill; user-scoped dialogue-memory systems, verifier-only systems, and parameter-training systems are outside the evaluation.

PoisonedEvolution transforms attacker-owned trajectories while preserving the original task and outcome and inserting an outcome-conditioned causal bridge that makes a target behavior appear useful for success or necessary to repair failure.

For SkillClaw, transformed records retain task-specific identifiers and successful outcomes while condensing history around a plausible workflow locus; for Trace2Skill, failed outcomes are retained and failure is attributed to the missing target behavior.

Domain-aligned placement supports Inclusion by locating the transformed behavior at plausible workflow points such as prerequisites, recovery, output transformation, or validation, without requiring knowledge of the private filter or evolver prompt.

Causal attribution is induced by repeatedly linking the target behavior to task-relevant constraints and observed outcomes, so the evolver sees a pattern analogous to requirement or obstacle → target behavior → task completion, or missing behavior → failure.

Cross-trajectory realization is encouraged by varying tasks and surface wording while keeping the operational semantics of the target behavior invariant, allowing the behavior to survive summarization, paraphrase, and skill merging.

The evaluation instantiates four representative security-effect families—confidentiality, data integrity, supply-chain integrity, and operational-safety weakening—using inert canary endpoints, paths, registries, and test flags without executing the referenced harmful actions.

The SkillClaw source corpus contains 300 case-level execution logs produced by GLM-5 using the original xlsx skill on 100 SpreadsheetBench training tasks, which were converted into SkillClaw-compatible sessions.

population.label: 300 case-level execution logs from 100 SpreadsheetBench training tasks

atoms.canonical_statement: Each SkillClaw trial constructs a task-distinct batch containing transformed attacker contributions and clean records, runs one native evolution cycle, and leaves the evolver prompt and skill-bank code unchanged so only selected input trajectories differ.

The main SkillClaw matrix uses the init refinement setting with n=30 trajectories, k=3 attacker records (10% support), 25 completed trials per model–family cell, six evolvers and four behavior families; optional session-quality judging and publish-time verification are disabled.
At 10% attacker support in the SkillClaw main matrix, PoisonedEvolution embedded target behaviors in 546 of 600 completed trials, corresponding to 91.0% SER.

population.label: SkillClaw init-setting evolution trials at n=30, k=3 across six evolvers and four behavior families

outcome.definition: Generated skill newly embeds the target behavior.

The Trace2Skill transfer experiment uses the full input path: each trial mixes three attacker-controlled, system-formatted failed trajectories with 27 clean failures from a held-out spreadsheet pool, then relies on native error analysis and skill consolidation; only the input trace pool changes.
The Trace2Skill transfer evaluation comprises 600 trials at n=30 and k=3 (10% attacker support), with 150 trials per security-effect family across multiple evolvers and evolution modes.
Across the Trace2Skill structural-transfer evaluation, PoisonedEvolution embedded target behavior in 369 of 600 trials (61.5% SER).

atoms.canonical_statement: The benign-task utility evaluation is a targeted sanity check and does not establish broad utility preservation or a complete utility–security trade-off under poisoning.

The pilot Provenance-Diversity Gate requires support from at least three users and clusters, rejects majority dominance, and penalizes high text overlap to distinguish concentrated provenance from independently supported evidence before promotion.

source_anchor.paragraph: Defenses should inspect evidence promotion, not only skill text

atoms.canonical_statement: SkillClaw results vary substantially by evolver, from 70.0% to 100.0% aggregate SER, showing that evolver policy is part of the attack surface; the authors caution that this is not a model quality or scale ranking.

The study evaluates one evolution cycle and does not measure whether a poisoned skill can create a longitudinal feedback loop by causing future trajectories to repeat and apparently revalidate the poisoned behavior.

source_anchor.paragraph: Evolution may create a feedback loop

atoms.canonical_statement: Artifact-origin provenance alone is insufficient because an authorized victim evolver can still produce a poisoned skill from attacker-controlled evidence; the authors argue that lineage should retain supporting and contradicting trajectories, contributor clusters, evolver version, and exact skill diff.

source_anchor.paragraph: Authentic provenance is not trustworthy provenance

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommend treating evidence promotion as a provenance-sensitive authorization decision and combining evidence-level promotion gates with pre-execution skill analysis, staged rollout, reversible skill versions, and capability-based runtime enforcement.

source_anchor.paragraph: Artifact poisoning and runtime impact are distinct

atoms.canonical_statement: The paper concludes that recurring, workflow-aligned adversarial evidence can satisfy Inclusion, Evolution Attribution, and Realization, making the experience-to-instruction promotion step a security boundary for self-evolving skill systems.
The authors conclude that defenses should apply provenance and relevance checks before experience becomes durable shared instruction rather than relying only on post-generation skill-text scanning.

extraction_limitations: The paper is an arXiv preprint and the extraction records source-reported claims without external verification.
The evaluation is artifact-level and does not establish runtime compromise, trigger activation, or real-world harmful action execution.
Trace2Skill is treated by the authors as a structural transfer case rather than an equal-sized benchmark target.
The provenance-diversity defense is a preliminary pilot with a small clean control and assumed candidate grouping.
No funding disclosure, conflict-of-interest statement, or dedicated data-availability statement was identified in the provided nine-page source; no atoms were fabricated for absent disclosures.
Related-work claims and bibliography entries were not atomized because they are provenance/context rather than original study findings.
